howThisFileWorks.userCount: Only USERCOUNT from the npm command sets headcount. Must be 50, 100, 150, 200 or another multiple of 50. Goals, tasks, and assessment bars all grow with N. Nothing here is a person cap.
howThisFileWorks.q2q4Weights: Five parts for scores 1-5. They add to 70. People per score = round_to_sum(M * weight / 70). Every score still gets some people. 4 and 5 are much larger so both rating averages stay above 4.5. Q2 and Q4 use different orders so the two charts do not match.
howThisFileWorks.checkboxWeights: Nine parts for nine options. They add to 210. Votes = M times 3. Other is the smallest slot. Q1, Q3, and Q5 shuffle the same parts so the three checkbox charts do not match. If Other is selected, otherNotesByQuestion is the required other_notes text for that question.
howThisFileWorks.otherNotesByQuestion: API 5 requires other_notes when Other is one of the three checkbox picks. These are the sentences a learner would type. Null when Other is not selected.
howThisFileWorks.goalSkills: At N=100, refGoals add to 90 and refGreen add to 60 for each person’s first goal. Scale with round_to_sum to M and A+B. B, C, and E then post a second goal on another of these 20 names. USERCOUNT people rotate job roles so many of these names can be posted.
howThisFileWorks.poolVsDefaults: USERCOUNT = dashboard variety. A and D get 1 goal; B, C, E get 2 so Goals set is higher than Users who set goals. Default full logins = 3 JSON goals each. Role and goal title stay matched on default logins.
howThisFileWorks.chats: Default full logins get meaningful 2 or 3 chats that match their job and goals in createDataInAiCoachForDefaultUsers, after at least one JSON goal, then one weekly session per chat. USERCOUNT pool chats run in createDataInAiCoachDashboard on the same N people: A–E one 2–3 turn chat from poolChatScripts after a successful goal, in batches of 20. F has no chat. Cycle scripts and durations separately. chatDurationsSeconds is the closed-block length, not wait time. The five values average 600 seconds so dashboard average conversation time is about 10 minutes.

poolProfile.keyResponsibilities: I do the core work of my role and keep the people around me unblocked.
poolProfile.careerAspiration: I want to grow in this role and take on harder problems.
poolProfile.motivation: I like finishing work that helps the team and the business.

q5Choices: Quality of work and attention to detail

IT Director.keyResponsibilities: I set technology direction and make sure our systems, security, and delivery teams stay aligned. I own budget, vendor choices, and the roadmap that keeps the business running. I also coach my managers so projects land on time.
IT Director.careerAspiration: I want to grow as a business-minded technology leader and get closer to company strategy. I would like to mentor more directors and tighten how we measure the value of tech work.
IT Director.motivation: I am energized when a messy platform problem becomes a clear plan and the teams execute it. Seeing the business trust technology as a partner keeps me going.

Learning and Development Specialist.keyResponsibilities: I design and run learning programs, work with managers on skill gaps, and keep content useful for the roles we support. I track completion and feedback so we know what to improve next.
Learning and Development Specialist.careerAspiration: I want to move into a learning-strategy role where I can shape career paths and skills programs for the whole org. I also want to get sharper at using data to prove learning impact.
Learning and Development Specialist.motivation: I like watching someone apply a new skill on the job. Building programs people actually use is what energizes me.

Infrastructure Engineer.keyResponsibilities: I keep servers, networks, and cloud environments stable and secure. I handle incidents, capacity, and automation so teams can ship without waiting on infrastructure.
Infrastructure Engineer.careerAspiration: I want to deepen cloud and reliability skills and grow into a senior or principal infrastructure role. I am also interested in platform work that other teams can self-serve.
Infrastructure Engineer.motivation: I am motivated when an outage is resolved cleanly or a manual process becomes a reliable pipeline. Quiet, stable systems are the win.

Data Architect.keyResponsibilities: I design how data is stored, modeled, and shared across products and reports. I set standards so analysts and engineers can trust what they query. I also review pipelines for quality and scale.
Data Architect.careerAspiration: I want to lead data strategy and mentor other architects. I would like to get stronger at turning business questions into simple, durable models.
Data Architect.motivation: I like bringing order to messy data and seeing a model get used in real decisions. Clarity for other teams is what drives me.

IT Support Specialist.keyResponsibilities: I help employees with access, devices, and day-to-day tech issues. I log tickets, find root causes, and write simple guides so the same problem does not keep coming back.
IT Support Specialist.careerAspiration: I want to grow into a senior support or systems role and get better at automation. I am also interested in moving toward infrastructure or endpoint management.
IT Support Specialist.motivation: I am energized when I unblock someone quickly and they can get back to work. Closing a tricky ticket for good is satisfying.

Software Engineer.keyResponsibilities: I design, build, and test product features with my squad. I review code, fix defects, and help keep our services reliable in production.
Software Engineer.careerAspiration: I want to grow into a senior engineer who can lead design and mentor others. I also want to get better at system design and shipping with less rework.
Software Engineer.motivation: I am motivated when a feature lands cleanly and customers can use it. Solving a hard bug with the team is what I enjoy most.

Retail Sales Associate.keyResponsibilities: I help shoppers find the right product, close sales, and keep the floor ready. I handle questions, returns, and simple follow-up so the store hits its daily goals.
Retail Sales Associate.careerAspiration: I want to grow into a shift lead or store supervisor and get stronger at coaching others on the floor. I am also interested in learning more about merchandising.
Retail Sales Associate.motivation: I like a busy floor and a customer who leaves happy. Hitting the day's target with the team energizes me.

Sales Associate.keyResponsibilities: I qualify leads, run conversations, and move opportunities through the pipeline. I keep notes accurate and follow up so nothing stalls after a good call.
Sales Associate.careerAspiration: I want to become a high-performing seller and then a team lead. I would like to get better at discovery and closing larger deals.
Sales Associate.motivation: I am motivated by a well-run conversation that turns into a real opportunity. Winning a deal we earned as a team keeps me going.

Production Operations Associate.keyResponsibilities: I keep daily production moving: schedules, handoffs, and quality checks. I flag delays early and work with the line so we meet output without cutting corners.
Production Operations Associate.careerAspiration: I want to grow into a production lead or supervisor and get stronger at planning and continuous improvement. I am also interested in safety and process design.
Production Operations Associate.motivation: I like a shift that finishes on plan. Fixing a bottleneck so the line runs smoothly is what energizes me.

Health and Safety Coordinator.keyResponsibilities: I run safety programs, walk the floor, and follow up on incidents and near misses. I train people on procedures and help managers close gaps before they become injuries.
Health and Safety Coordinator.careerAspiration: I want to grow into a broader EHS or operations-risk role. I would like to get better at using incident data to prevent the next event, not only report the last one.
Health and Safety Coordinator.motivation: I am motivated when a site is safer because we changed a habit, not only a policy. People going home well is the point.

Customer Success Manager.keyResponsibilities: I own post-sale relationships, adoption, and renewals for my accounts. I run check-ins, surface risks early, and pull in the right internal people when a customer is stuck.
Customer Success Manager.careerAspiration: I want to grow into a senior CSM or team lead and get stronger at expansion conversations. I also want to use customer data more, not only relationship notes.
Customer Success Manager.motivation: I like turning a worried customer into a confident one. A renewal we earned through real value is what drives me.

Channel Sales Manager.keyResponsibilities: I grow revenue through partners: enablement, pipeline, and deal support. I keep partner expectations clear and remove blockers so they can sell with us.
Channel Sales Manager.careerAspiration: I want to lead a larger partner motion and get better at picking which channels to invest in. I am also interested in partner-led growth strategy.
Channel Sales Manager.motivation: I am energized when a partner closes a deal we coached well. Seeing two companies win together keeps me going.

Sales Director.keyResponsibilities: I set the sales plan, coach managers, and own the number for my region or segment. I review pipeline quality, hire and develop sellers, and keep forecast honest.
Sales Director.careerAspiration: I want to grow into a broader commercial leadership role and get sharper at building repeatable teams, not only individual heroes. I also want to tighten how we use data in forecast.
Sales Director.motivation: I am motivated when the team hits a hard number the right way. Developing a seller who starts to win on their own is the best part.

VP Technology.keyResponsibilities: I own technology strategy, investment choices, and how engineering and IT support the business. I align leaders on priorities, risk, and delivery. I also grow the next layer of tech leadership.
VP Technology.careerAspiration: I want to keep getting better at connecting technology bets to company outcomes. I would like to build a stronger leadership bench and a simpler operating model.
VP Technology.motivation: I am energized when a hard tradeoff becomes a clear decision and the organization moves. Seeing teams ship with less friction is what I care about.

I am not sure which skill to work on first.
Give me one small step I can take this week.

I need a simple way to pick what matters today.
What should I try in my next 1:1 with my manager?
I want to speak up more in team meetings.
I freeze when I have to explain a decision.
Help me practice one clear sentence I can use.
I finished a task but I am not sure it was the right one.
How do I check that my work actually helps the team?
Give me two questions I can ask before I start the next task.

Production changes still feel risky on my team.

I need to plan next-quarter capacity before we run out of headroom.
I will inventory host and disk use for the top 20 services and share a forecast with managers.
Our reports keep arguing about the same company metrics.
I want a glossary with name, owner, and grain for five core metrics.
Then I will flag two dashboards that disagree and name the source of truth.
I need to draw the target data platform so we stop adding one-off pipelines.
I will sketch current vs target flows and list three bets for next year: what we build, what we stop, and why.
We keep taking stories that cannot finish in one sprint.
I want to break the next story into a demo-able slice, not a half-built epic.

I want to use AI on code without leaking secrets from prod or tickets.
I will write a safe-prompt checklist and keep any assistant diff small enough to review like a normal PR.

I want to speed up boilerplate with generative AI without skipping review.

Shoppers stall because I start with a discount instead of what they need.

Returns and busy hours still get tense.

The evening team misses what I saw at close.

My discovery calls jump to product before I know need, budget, and timing.

Stuck deals stall because SE, manager, or legal hear too late.
I will list who I pull in and when, and send a weekly note on three live deals and what I need from each person.
The line keeps waiting in the same place and we miss the shift plan.
